fidelity: F2a — BEM-derived Cp(lambda,beta) + rotor-dynamics ODE + PMSG load
source: Manwell, McGowan & Rogers (2009) Wind Energy Explained 2nd ed. (BEM, Ch.3); Burton et al. (2011) Wind Energy Handbook 2nd ed.; Heier (2014) Grid Integration of Wind Energy 3rd ed. (Cp(lambda,beta) fit); IEC 61400-2:2013 (small wind turbines); Wood (2011) Small Wind Turbines (low-Re, furling)

unit.name: Generic 10 kW Small Wind Turbine (Bergey Excel 10 class), 3-blade HAWT + direct-drive PMSG

rho.note: Air density at sea level, 15 C (ISA)

Cp_max.note: Peak rotor power coefficient. Small HAWTs run below the 0.45-0.50 of utility rotors because of low blade Reynolds number (Re~1e5) and tip/root losses (Wood 2011; IEC 61400-2). Stays below Betz 16/27=0.593.

lambda_opt.note: Tip-speed ratio at peak Cp for a 3-blade small HAWT (Manwell 2009)

J_rotor.note: Combined rotor+drivetrain inertia referred to the rotor shaft (direct-drive small HAWT, ~3.5 m blades). Order-of-magnitude per Burton et al. (2011).

T_loss_coeff.note: Viscous/bearing+windage loss torque coefficient: T_loss = b*omega (Manwell 2009 drivetrain loss). Small vs aero torque (~hundreds N.m) so operating point stays near lambda_opt.

kt_gen.note: PMSG torque constant (= flux linkage * pole pairs * 3/2). Direct-drive small machine.

K_opt_torque.note: Optimal-torque control gain K = 0.5*rho*A*Cp_max*R^3/lambda_opt^3 (Bossanyi optimal TSR tracking, Burton 2011 eq. for K_opt). T_gen = K*omega^2 below rated; at this gain T_aero = K*omega^2 exactly at lambda_opt, so the rotor settles at the peak-Cp tip-speed ratio. For D=7,Cp_max=0.40,lambda_opt=7 -> 1.179.

omega_rated.note: Rotor speed at rated wind v_rated=11 m/s (omega = lambda_opt*v_rated/R = 22 rad/s ~ 210 rpm).

v_furl.note: Wind speed at which passive furling/over-speed protection begins to shed area (small HAWT tail-furling, Wood 2011).

v_cut_out.note: Cut-out wind speed; rotor fully furled above this (F1b).

furl_exponent.note: Sharpness of the furling area-reduction roll-off between v_furl and v_cut_out.

TI_ref.note: Representative turbulence intensity for small turbines in the built/near-ground environment (IEC 61400-2 NTM is higher than 61400-1).
